title: Ecclesiastes 3 — A time for everything under the skies

verdicts.reasoning: lakkōl zĕmān wĕʿēt lĕkol-ḥēpeṣ taḥat haššāmāyim: 'under the skies' (Qohelet's variant of 'under the sun'); late-Hebrew ḥēpeṣ 'matter'; setumot kept. Exact.
Re-parsed: ʿēt lāledet wĕʿēt lāmût ʿēt lāṭaʿat wĕʿēt laʿăqôr nāṭûaʿ. Infinitive antitheses rendered in order, one English verb per Hebrew verb. Exact.
Re-parsed: ʿēt lahărôg wĕʿēt lirpôʾ ʿēt lipĕrôṣ wĕʿēt libnôt. Infinitive antitheses rendered in order, one English verb per Hebrew verb. Exact.
Re-parsed: ʿēt libkôt wĕʿēt liśḥôq ʿēt sĕpôd wĕʿēt rĕqôd. Infinitive antitheses rendered in order, one English verb per Hebrew verb. Exact.
Re-parsed: ʿēt lĕhašlîk ʾăbānîm wĕʿēt kĕnôs ʾăbānîm ... lirḥōq mēḥabbēq. Infinitive antitheses rendered in order, one English verb per Hebrew verb. Exact.
Re-parsed: ʿēt lĕbaqqēš wĕʿēt lĕʾabbēd ʿēt lišmôr wĕʿēt lĕhašlîk. Infinitive antitheses rendered in order, one English verb per Hebrew verb. Exact.
Re-parsed: ʿēt liqrôaʿ wĕʿēt litpôr ʿēt laḥăšôt wĕʿēt lĕdabbēr. Infinitive antitheses rendered in order, one English verb per Hebrew verb. Exact.
Re-parsed: ʿēt leʾĕhōb wĕʿēt liśnōʾ ʿēt milḥāmâ wĕʿēt šālôm. Infinitive antitheses rendered in order, one English verb per Hebrew verb. Exact.
mah-yyitrôn hāʿôśeh baʾăšer hûʾ ʿāmēl: yitrôn 'gain' (key word; ASV 'profit' recorded). Exact.
rāʾîtî ʾet-hāʿinyān ʾăšer nātan ʾĕlōhîm libnê hāʾādām laʿănôt bô: anarthrous 'Elohim', 'the sons of the human' (founder point B). The changed line was verified.

Re-parsed: ʾet-hakkōl ʿāśâ yāpeh bĕʿittô gam ʾet-hāʿōlām nātan bĕlibbām ...: hāʿōlām 'eternity' (ASV, NRSV, NJPS), with 'world' (Vulgate/KJV) and the repointing hāʿelem recorded; articular 'the Elohim'. Defensible.
yādaʿtî kî ʾên ṭôb bām kî ʾim-liśmôaḥ wĕlaʿăśôt ṭôb bĕḥayyāyw: the generalizing 'in one's life' is declared. Exact.
wĕgam kol-hāʾādām šeyyōʾkal wĕšātâ ... mattat ʾĕlōhîm hîʾ: 'every human'; anarthrous 'Elohim'. Exact.
yādaʿtî kî kol-ʾăšer yaʿăśeh hāʾĕlōhîm hûʾ yihyeh lĕʿôlām ...: articular 'the Elohim' with singular verbs. Exact.

mah-šehāyâ kĕbār hûʾ waʾăšer lihyôt kĕbār hāyâ wĕhāʾĕlōhîm yĕbaqqēš ʾet-nirdāp: ASV/NRSV construal, with the word-order construal (the canon's) recorded; literal 'what has been driven away' for nirdāp. Source-honest.
wĕʿôd rāʾîtî taḥat haššemeš mĕqôm hammišpāṭ šāmmâ hārešaʿ ...: the Hebrew repetition is kept. Exact.
ʾāmartî ʾănî bĕlibbî ... kî-ʿēt lĕkol-ḥēpeṣ wĕʿal kol-hammaʿăśeh šām: MT šām 'there' (ASV) kept, emendation śām recorded; internal speech introduced by a colon. Exact.
ʿal-dibrat bĕnê hāʾādām lĕbārām hāʾĕlōhîm wĕlirʾôt šĕhem-bĕhēmâ hēmmâ lāhem: brr 'test'; no ASV supplement. The changed line was verified.

citations: Fox, A Time to Tear Down and a Time to Build Up (1999), on hebel
verdicts.reasoning: kî miqreh bĕnê-hāʾādām ûmiqreh habbĕhēmâ ... wĕrûaḥ ʾeḥād lakkōl ... kî hakkōl hābel: one breath (ASV 'breath'), 'vanity' with the alternatives in hevel-vanity-ecclesiastes. The canon quotes the verse closely, and the line follows the Hebrew. Changed line ('the sons of the human') verified.
hakkōl hôlēk ʾel-māqôm ʾeḥād hakkōl hāyâ min-heʿāpār wĕhakkōl šāb ʾel-heʿāpār. Exact (Gen 3:19 echo noted).

citations: LXX Eccl 3:21 ei anabainei; Vulgate si ascendat
verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed: mî yôdēaʿ rûaḥ bĕnê hāʾādām hāʿōlâ hîʾ lĕmāʿĕlâ wĕrûaḥ habbĕhēmâ hayyōredet hîʾ lĕmaṭṭâ lāʾāreṣ. Source checked: the MT points both participles with the article. Translating that pointing ('that goes upward ... that goes downward') is the declared MT baseline and is grammatical. The KJV also follows it ('the spirit of man that goeth upward'), so the line is not without English precedent. The interrogative reading of the LXX (ei), Vulgate (si), ASV, NRSV and NJPS is fully set out. 'breath' in both halves continues v 19 (NJPS 'lifebreath'; BDB rûaḥ 'breath of life'). Non-blocking: add the KJV to the note as the English witness to the Masoretic pointing.
wĕrāʾîtî kî ʾên ṭôb mēʾăšer yiśmaḥ hāʾādām bĕmaʿăśāyw ...: 'the human'; final question literal. Exact.

glossaryReview.reasoning: Every site verified: YHWH; 'Yah' (Ps 147:1, 20); the article follows the Hebrew (anarthrous Ps 8:6; Eccl 3:10, 13; articular Eccl 3:11, 14, 15, 17, 18); 'El', 'Eloah' and 'Shaddai' as in stable job-woh (38:41; 40:2, 9); 'our Lord' for ʾădōnênû. Direct is right: these are presentation rules over explicit Hebrew forms. Flagged only for founder point A (Ps 8:6 'Elohim' against the canon's 'the Elohim'). Reviewer view: keep the anarthrous form. The Hebrew has no article, the rule matches job-woh 1:9 and the Kings clause 2, and departing from the canon's wording here is evidence that the line is not canon-driven.

Site-by-site application of the founder's Kings-wave register ruling, checked verse by verse: physical sky 'skies' (Ps 8:2, 4, 9; 19:2, 7; 33:6; 147:8; Prov 8:27; Eccl 3:1; Job 37:3); dwelling or cosmic height 'heavens' (Ps 33:13 || mĕkôn-šibtô; 139:8 against She'ol). Ps 8:2 ('splendor upon the skies') is the closest call and is argued from v 4. Direct is appropriate.

'earth' at universal and cosmic sites (kol-hāʾāreṣ; ʾereṣ || tēbēl) is the reading of ASV, NRSV and NJPS, and the isaiah-woh precedent. 'land' is kept for territory (Prov 10:30; Job 37:13) and the stable 'wings of the land' (Job 37:3 = 38:13). Every site was checked. Agree with founder point C: promote the clause to central eretz in a later diff.

The lexical mapping is accurate and consistent with central ha-adam / ben-adam (direct) and with GEN-WOH-11:5 'the sons of the human' (checked). ʾĕnôš 'a mortal' and ʾîšîm 'O men' are sound. Flagged for founder point B. The articular/anarthrous split ('the sons of the human' / 'the sons of human', Prov 8:4, 31) is formally exact but yields stiff English, and in Biblical Hebrew the two forms are not distinct in sense. The corpus is now split three ways ('sons of men' ASV / canon-EN; 'children of men' 1 Kgs 8:39; 'sons of the human' Gen 11:5). Reviewer view: accept the editor's forms for coherence with the central entries, and align 1 Kgs 8:39 to them. If the founder prefers idiom, revert all bĕnê (hā)ʾādām sites together to 'the sons of men' with a string swap, and leave the singular ben-adam untouched.

Inferred is the honest class: the traditional English of Eccl 3:21 is 'spirit'. The lexical evidence is real. BDB and HALOT give rûaḥ 'breath (of life)'; NJPS has 'lifebreath' at Eccl 3:21; and vv 19-21 argue about the one rûaḥ that humans and beasts share (Gen 6:17; 7:15, 22). Lower-case 'spirit' at Ps 139:7 follows NRSV and NJPS. 'wind' (Job 37:21; Ps 147:18) and 'breath of his mouth' (Ps 33:6) are uncontroversial.

Applied correctly at every listed site. MT Psalm numbering was verified (superscription = v 1 in Pss 8, 19; run into v 1 in Ps 139). The one vowel-only exception at Ps 8:2 is declared and justified: the MT impv. tĕnâ has no syntax after ʾăšer. Eccl 3:21 keeps the Masoretic articular participles and fully records the interrogative reading of LXX, Vulgate, ASV, NRSV and NJPS. Non-blocking: add 'KJV' to the Eccl 3:21 clause as the English witness to the MT pointing ('the spirit of man that goeth upward'), so that the entry does not suggest that every English version departs from the MT.

The Hebrew mēʾĕlōhîm is anarthrous, the rule matches job-woh 1:9 and Kings clause 2, and the reception note already gives the canon's 'the Elohim'. paragraphs.text: לַכֹּ֖ל זְמָ֑ן וְעֵ֥ת לְכָל־חֵ֖פֶץ תַּ֥חַת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: For everything there is a season, and a time for every matter under the skies:

notes.official: *lakkōl zĕmān wĕʿēt lĕkol-ḥēpeṣ taḥat haššāmāyim* 'For everything there is a season, and a time for every matter under the skies'. *taḥat haššāmayim* (1:13; 2:3) is Qohelet's variant of *taḥat haššemeš* 'under the sun' (v 16) and names the world under the visible sky, so 'skies' (central `shamayim`; ASV 'under heaven'). *ḥēpeṣ* 'delight, desire' has in late Hebrew the sense 'matter, affair' (ASV 'purpose'). The setumot (ס) after vv 1 and 8 stay in the Hebrew text; v 1 ends with a colon that introduces the list of vv 2-8. Ecclesiastes is new in the corpus; the Writings conventions apply (`poetic-lineation-and-speech-convention-writings`).

paragraphs.text: עֵ֥ת לָלֶ֖דֶת וְעֵ֣ת לָמ֑וּת עֵ֣ת לָטַ֔עַת וְעֵ֖ת לַעֲק֥וֹר נָטֽוּעַ׃

i18n.en: a time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to uproot what is planted;

notes.official: The fourteen pairs of vv 2-8 set infinitives in antithesis. *ʿēt lāledet* 'a time to be born' (the infinitive can also be active, 'to give birth'); *laʿăqôr nāṭûaʿ* 'to uproot what is planted'.

paragraphs.text: עֵ֤ת לַהֲרוֹג֙ וְעֵ֣ת לִרְפּ֔וֹא עֵ֥ת לִפְר֖וֹץ וְעֵ֥ת לִבְנֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: a time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;

paragraphs.text: עֵ֤ת לִבְכּוֹת֙ וְעֵ֣ת לִשְׂח֔וֹק עֵ֥ת סְפ֖וֹד וְעֵ֥ת רְקֽוֹד׃

i18n.en: a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;

paragraphs.text: עֵ֚ת לְהַשְׁלִ֣יךְ אֲבָנִ֔ים וְעֵ֖ת כְּנ֣וֹס אֲבָנִ֑ים עֵ֣ת לַחֲב֔וֹק וְעֵ֖ת לִרְחֹ֥ק מֵחַבֵּֽק׃

i18n.en: a time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;

notes.official: *lĕhašlîk ʾăbānîm ... kĕnôs ʾăbānîm* 'to cast away stones ... to gather stones together'. The image is not explained in the text. Proposals include clearing a field and building (cf. 2 Kgs 3:19, 25); the Midrash (Qohelet Rabbah) reads it of marital relations, which the second half would then continue.

paragraphs.text: עֵ֤ת לְבַקֵּשׁ֙ וְעֵ֣ת לְאַבֵּ֔ד עֵ֥ת לִשְׁמ֖וֹר וְעֵ֥ת לְהַשְׁלִֽיךְ׃

i18n.en: a time to seek, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;

paragraphs.text: עֵ֤ת לִקְר֙וֹעַ֙ וְעֵ֣ת לִתְפּ֔וֹר עֵ֥ת לַחֲשׁ֖וֹת וְעֵ֥ת לְדַבֵּֽר׃

i18n.en: a time to tear, and a time to sew; a time to keep silent, and a time to speak;

paragraphs.text: עֵ֤ת לֶֽאֱהֹב֙ וְעֵ֣ת לִשְׂנֹ֔א עֵ֥ת מִלְחָמָ֖ה וְעֵ֥ת שָׁלֽוֹם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: a time to love, and a time to hate; a time for war, and a time for peace.

paragraphs.text: מַה־יִּתְרוֹן֙ הָֽעוֹשֶׂ֔ה בַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר ה֥וּא עָמֵֽל׃

i18n.en: What gain has the worker in that in which he toils?

notes.official: *mah-yitrôn hāʿôśeh baʾăšer hûʾ ʿāmēl* 'What gain has the worker in that in which he toils?': *yitrôn* 'gain, advantage' (1:3) is one of Qohelet's key words (ASV 'profit').

paragraphs.text: רָאִ֣יתִי אֶת־הָֽעִנְיָ֗ן אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֧ן אֱלֹהִ֛ים לִבְנֵ֥י הָאָדָ֖ם לַעֲנ֥וֹת בּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: I have seen the task that Elohim has given to the sons of the human to be occupied with.

notes.official: *rāʾîtî ʾet-hāʿinyān ʾăšer nātan ʾĕlōhîm libnê hāʾādām laʿănôt bô* 'I have seen the task that Elohim has given to the sons of the human to be occupied with' (cf. 1:13). Ecclesiastes alternates anarthrous *ʾĕlōhîm* (vv 10, 13) with *hāʾĕlōhîm* (vv 11, 14, 15, 17, 18). The English follows the Hebrew article, 'Elohim' / 'the Elohim', with the singular verbs and pronouns of the Hebrew (`elohim-as-translation`; `divine-names-convention-writings`). *bĕnê hāʾādām* is 'the sons of the human' (central `ha-adam`, as genesis-woh 11:5; ASV 'the sons of men'), and *hāʾādām* alone is 'the human' (vv 11, 19, 22; `adam-enosh-ish-human-terms-writings`). *ʿinyān* 'task, business' (ASV 'travail').

paragraphs.text: אֶת־הַכֹּ֥ל עָשָׂ֖ה יָפֶ֣ה בְעִתּ֑וֹ גַּ֤ם אֶת־הָעֹלָם֙ נָתַ֣ן בְּלִבָּ֔ם מִבְּלִ֞י אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹא־יִמְצָ֣א הָאָדָ֗ם אֶת־הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֥ה הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים מֵרֹ֥אשׁ וְעַד־סֽוֹף׃

i18n.en: He has made everything beautiful in its time; also he has set eternity in their heart, yet so that the human cannot find out the work that the Elohim has done from the beginning to the end.

notes.official: *ʾet-hakkōl ʿāśâ yāpeh bĕʿittô* 'He has made everything beautiful in its time'. *gam ʾet-hāʿōlām nātan bĕlibbām* 'also he has set eternity in their heart': *hāʿōlām* is 'eternity' (ASV, NRSV, NJPS). The post-biblical sense 'the world' (Vulgate *mundum*, KJV) and the repointing *hāʿelem* 'what is hidden, ignorance' are recorded in `ha-olam-eternity-ecclesiastes-3-11`. *mibbĕlî ʾăšer lōʾ-yimṣāʾ hāʾādām* 'yet so that the human cannot find out' (ASV) 'the work that the Elohim has done from the beginning to the end'.

paragraphs.text: יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין ט֖וֹב בָּ֑ם כִּ֣י אִם־לִשְׂמ֔וֹחַ וְלַעֲשׂ֥וֹת ט֖וֹב בְּחַיָּֽיו׃

i18n.en: I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and to do good in one's life;

notes.official: *kî ʾên ṭôb bām* 'that there is nothing better for them'; *bĕḥayyāyw* 'in his life', generalized in English to 'in one's life'.

paragraphs.text: וְגַ֤ם כָּל־הָאָדָם֙ שֶׁיֹּאכַ֣ל וְשָׁתָ֔ה וְרָאָ֥ה ט֖וֹב בְּכָל־עֲמָל֑וֹ מַתַּ֥ת אֱלֹהִ֖ים הִֽיא׃

i18n.en: and also that every human should eat and drink and see good in all his toil — it is the gift of Elohim.

notes.official: *wĕgam kol-hāʾādām* 'and also that every human' (`ha-adam`); *mattat ʾĕlōhîm hîʾ* 'it is the gift of Elohim' (anarthrous; `elohim-as-translation`).

paragraphs.text: יָדַ֗עְתִּי כִּ֠י כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַעֲשֶׂ֤ה הָאֱלֹהִים֙ ה֚וּא יִהְיֶ֣ה לְעוֹלָ֔ם עָלָיו֙ אֵ֣ין לְהוֹסִ֔יף וּמִמֶּ֖נּוּ אֵ֣ין לִגְרֹ֑עַ וְהָאֱלֹהִ֣ים עָשָׂ֔ה שֶׁיִּֽרְא֖וּ מִלְּפָנָֽיו׃

i18n.en: I know that whatever the Elohim does, it will be forever; nothing can be added to it, and nothing taken from it; and the Elohim has done it, so that they should fear before him.

notes.official: *kol-ʾăšer yaʿăśeh hāʾĕlōhîm hûʾ yihyeh lĕʿôlām* 'whatever the Elohim does, it will be forever' (articular). *ʿālāyw ʾên lĕhôsîp ûmimmennû ʾên ligrōaʿ* 'nothing can be added to it, and nothing taken from it' (cf. Deut 4:2; 13:1). *šeyyirʾû millĕpānāyw* 'so that they should fear before him'.

paragraphs.text: מַה־שֶּֽׁהָיָה֙ כְּבָ֣ר ה֔וּא וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לִהְי֖וֹת כְּבָ֣ר הָיָ֑ה וְהָאֱלֹהִ֖ים יְבַקֵּ֥שׁ אֶת־נִרְדָּֽף׃

i18n.en: That which is has already been, and that which is to be has already been; and the Elohim seeks what has been driven away.

notes.official:
*mah-šehāyâ kĕbār hûʾ waʾăšer lihyôt kĕbār hāyâ* 'That which is has already been, and that which is to be has already been' (ASV and NRSV construal). The first clause can also be read in its word order, 'What has been, already is' (cf. 1:9). *wĕhāʾĕlōhîm yĕbaqqēš ʾet-nirdāp* 'and the Elohim seeks what has been driven away': *nirdāp* is 'the pursued' (NJPS 'God seeks the pursued'), often taken as the past that has gone by (ASV 'that which is passed away'); the line keeps the literal participle.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes the first half in the word-order construal ('Ce qui déjà fut est et ce qui doit être a déjà été'; English 'That which hath been is now; and that which is to be hath already been') and connects it with the cycle in which created beings in turn create others. Both construals say that what will be has been before; the line follows the ASV construal.

paragraphs.text: וְע֥וֹד רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ מְק֤וֹם הַמִּשְׁפָּט֙ שָׁ֣מָּה הָרֶ֔שַׁע וּמְק֥וֹם הַצֶּ֖דֶק שָׁ֥מָּה הָרָֽשַׁע׃

i18n.en: And moreover I saw under the sun: in the place of justice, there was wickedness; and in the place of righteousness, there was wickedness.

notes.official: *taḥat haššemeš* 'under the sun'; *mĕqôm hammišpāṭ šāmmâ hārešaʿ* 'in the place of justice, there was wickedness'. The repetition in the second half is the Hebrew's.

paragraphs.text: אָמַ֤רְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ בְּלִבִּ֔י אֶת־הַצַּדִּיק֙ וְאֶת־הָ֣רָשָׁ֔ע יִשְׁפֹּ֖ט הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּי־עֵ֣ת לְכָל־חֵ֔פֶץ וְעַ֥ל כָּל־הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה שָֽׁם׃

i18n.en: I said in my heart: the Elohim will judge the righteous and the wicked, for there is a time there for every matter and for every work.

notes.official: *ʾāmartî ʾănî bĕlibbî* 'I said in my heart': internal speech, introduced with a colon and no quotation marks (`poetic-lineation-and-speech-convention-writings`). *hāʾĕlōhîm* 'the Elohim' (articular). *kî-ʿēt lĕkol-ḥēpeṣ wĕʿal kol-hammaʿăśeh šām* 'for there is a time there for every matter and for every work': MT *šām* 'there' (ASV). Many emend to *śām* 'he has appointed (a time)'. The MT is translated (`mt-baseline-versification-and-psalm-numbering-writings`).

paragraphs.text: אָמַ֤רְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ בְּלִבִּ֔י עַל־דִּבְרַת֙ בְּנֵ֣י הָאָדָ֔ם לְבָרָ֖ם הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְלִרְא֕וֹת שְׁהֶם־בְּהֵמָ֥ה הֵ֖מָּה לָהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: I said in my heart concerning the sons of the human: that the Elohim may test them, and that they may see that they themselves are beasts.

notes.official: *ʿal-dibrat bĕnê hāʾādām* 'concerning the sons of the human' (`ha-adam`); *lĕbārām hāʾĕlōhîm* 'that the Elohim may test them' (*brr* 'sift, purify'; ASV 'prove'). *šĕhem-bĕhēmâ hēmmâ lāhem* 'that they themselves are beasts' (the ASV supplies '[but as]').

paragraphs.text: כִּי֩ מִקְרֶ֨ה בְֽנֵי־הָאָדָ֜ם וּמִקְרֶ֣ה הַבְּהֵמָ֗ה וּמִקְרֶ֤ה אֶחָד֙ לָהֶ֔ם כְּמ֥וֹת זֶה֙ כֵּ֣ן מ֣וֹת זֶ֔ה וְר֥וּחַ אֶחָ֖ד לַכֹּ֑ל וּמוֹתַ֨ר הָאָדָ֤ם מִן־הַבְּהֵמָה֙ אָ֔יִן כִּ֥י הַכֹּ֖ל הָֽבֶל׃

i18n.en: For what befalls the sons of the human and what befalls the beast — one and the same thing befalls them: as the one dies, so dies the other; they all have one breath, and the human has no advantage over the beast, for all is vanity.

notes.official:
*kî miqreh bĕnê-hāʾādām ûmiqreh habbĕhēmâ ûmiqreh ʾeḥād lāhem* 'For what befalls the sons of the human and what befalls the beast — one and the same thing befalls them'. *wĕrûaḥ ʾeḥād lakkōl* 'they all have one breath': *rûaḥ* is the breath of life that humans and animals share (Gen 6:17; 7:15, 22; `ruach-wind-breath-spirit-writings`). *ûmôtar hāʾādām min-habbĕhēmâ ʾāyin* 'and the human has no advantage over the beast'. *kî hakkōl hābel* 'for all is vanity': *hebel* is literally 'breath, vapour', Qohelet's leitmotif. The line keeps the ASV 'vanity' and records the alternatives ('futility', 'mere breath', 'absurd') in `hevel-vanity-ecclesiastes`. The central `hevel` entry governs the personal name Hevel (Abel), the same word, in Gen 4.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes the verse ('A man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all is vanity') and reads it as saying that the animals too were created and will be recreated, just like humans, neither more nor less. The line renders the Hebrew, which the canon's wording follows closely.

paragraphs.text: הַכֹּ֥ל הוֹלֵ֖ךְ אֶל־מָק֣וֹם אֶחָ֑ד הַכֹּל֙ הָיָ֣ה מִן־הֶֽעָפָ֔ר וְהַכֹּ֖ל שָׁ֥ב אֶל־הֶעָפָֽר׃

i18n.en: All go to one place; all are from the dust, and all return to the dust.

notes.official: *hakkōl hôlēk ʾel-māqôm ʾeḥād* 'All go to one place'; *min-heʿāpār ... ʾel-heʿāpār* 'from the dust ... to the dust' (Gen 3:19).

paragraphs.text: מִ֣י יוֹדֵ֗עַ ר֚וּחַ בְּנֵ֣י הָאָדָ֔ם הָעֹלָ֥ה הִ֖יא לְמָ֑עְלָה וְר֙וּחַ֙ הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה הַיֹּרֶ֥דֶת הִ֖יא לְמַ֥טָּה לָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: Who knows the breath of the sons of the human that goes upward, and the breath of the beast that goes downward to the earth?

notes.official: *mî yôdēaʿ rûaḥ bĕnê hāʾādām hāʿōlâ hîʾ lĕmāʿĕlâ* 'Who knows the breath of the sons of the human that goes upward, and the breath of the beast that goes downward to the earth?' The MT points both participles with the article (*hāʿōlâ*, *hayyōredet*): 'that goes upward ... that goes downward'. The consonants also allow the interrogative *hă-* ('whether it goes upward ... whether it goes downward'), which the LXX, the Vulgate, the ASV, NRSV and NJPS read; the KJV follows the MT pointing ('the spirit of man that goeth upward'). The MT pointing is translated and the versional reading recorded (`mt-baseline-versification-and-psalm-numbering-writings`). *rûaḥ* is 'breath' in both halves and as in v 19, because vv 19-21 argue about the one breath that humans and beasts share (ASV 'spirit'; NJPS 'lifebreath'; `ruach-wind-breath-spirit-writings`). *lāʾāreṣ* 'to the earth', the ground below (`eretz-earth-and-land-scope-writings`).

paragraphs.text: וְרָאִ֗יתִי כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין טוֹב֙ מֵאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׂמַ֤ח הָאָדָם֙ בְּֽמַעֲשָׂ֔יו כִּי־ה֖וּא חֶלְק֑וֹ כִּ֣י מִ֤י יְבִיאֶ֙נּוּ֙ לִרְא֔וֹת בְּמֶ֖ה שֶׁיִּהְיֶ֥ה אַחֲרָֽיו׃

i18n.en: So I saw that there is nothing better than that the human should rejoice in his works, for that is his portion; for who will bring him to see what will be after him?

notes.official: *ʾên ṭôb mēʾăšer yiśmaḥ hāʾādām bĕmaʿăśāyw* 'there is nothing better than that the human should rejoice in his works'; *kî-hûʾ ḥelqô* 'for that is his portion'; *mî yĕbîʾennû lirʾôt bĕmeh šeyyihyeh ʾaḥărāyw* 'who will bring him to see what will be after him?'
